objective: Test whether task-held-out linear and nonlinear predictability survives removal of prompt-surface variance without exposing held-out tasks to the nuisance model.
estimand: Change in task-held-out probe accuracy and macro-F1 after fold-local prompt-surface residualization, reported beside the unadjusted probe.
feature_scope: Prompt-only. Targets, correctness, generated responses, and output length are excluded because they occur after the prefill representation being analyzed.

residualizer.standardization: Fit nuisance-column mean and scale on training tasks only; constant columns retain unit scale.
residualizer.fit_scope: Refit inside every task-held-out fold for the observed assignment and every task-label permutation.
residualizer.order: Ridge residualization, then fold-local PCA for the cuML estimator family, then probe scaling and classification.

inference.multiple_testing: Benjamini-Hochberg separately for each adjusted probe metric across layer-stream rows

decision_rule: A result is more resistant to measured prompt-surface confounding only when adjusted task-held-out performance and corrected permutation evidence persist. Residual predictability is not proof of a knowledge-versus-reasoning mechanism because domain, difficulty, and unmeasured format features remain.
prohibited_covariates: task or dataset identity, because it cannot generalize to held-out tasks
class label or any deterministic transform of it
generated response or output length for this prefill analysis
